Just one-third of patients prescribed new medicines filled them within 30 days, with a new report from the Institute for Clinical and Economic Review and West Health suggesting that cost is the problem.
Despite the White House’s efforts to cut drug prices, the biopharma industry continues to launch new medicines that cost in excess of $250,000, putting further strain on the U.S. healthcare system, according to a drug pricing watchdog.
The median net launch price, which is the price paid after rebates and discounts, increased by 35% from $190,000 in 2022 to $257,000 in 2025, according to a new report from the Institute for Clinical and Economic Review (ICER) and West Health. Prices have remained “at historically high levels,” the firms said in an accompanying release.
And about one in four drugs launched in 2025 exceeded $500,000 in annual net price, according to the report. Another 34% had prices between $200,000 and $500,000.
“This independent analysis shows that we are facing a critical moment in the U.S. health care system,” Sarah Emond, president of ICER, an independent group that monitors drug pricing, said in a Tuesday statement .
President Donald Trump has made drug pricing a key policy of his second term, rolling out Most Favored Nation drug pricing that seeks to match costs with other comparable nations. But the policy has affected just a handful of specific drugs, and many experts have questioned the impact.
The ICER report includes about 50 drugs that have recently launched. On the list is Vertex Pharmaceuticals’ non-opioid pain drug Journavx, Eli Lilly’s Alzheimer’s treatment Kisunla and BridgeBio Pharma’s Attruby for transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM), among others.
Not only can the high costs of these drugs put a strain on the patient and the healthcare system, they can also result in unfilled prescriptions, cutting into the manufacturers’ bottom lines. Just one-third of patients prescribed these new medicines actually filled them and picked them up within 30 days, with a significant portion of these unfilled prescriptions resulting from a lack of insurance coverage in the early days following approval, ICER said.
ICER took a closer look at a few select drugs, including Eli Lilly’s recently launched Ebglyss for atopic dermatitis. The therapy has a net price of $41,622, with fairly high Medicaid fill rates of 54%, compared to just 27% for patients going through commercial payers. Fill rate is when a patient orders the prescription, it’s approved and they are able to pick it up.
The watchdog believes that the drug was likely rejected by payers because of the many other options available for atopic dermatitis, a common but stubborn skin condition that causes dry, itchy and inflamed skin.
Medicare had the highest overall rate of rejection, the report stated. These prescriptions included out-of-pocket payments for patients, with about 20% paying $500 or more and 15% over $1,500 per month.
The fill rate for Journavx was 55% of the 251,696 patients who received a prescription. The therapy is available to those with coverage for as little as $2 but self-pay consumers could pay as much as $500 for a month’s supply.
“Overpayment for drugs beyond their value to patients is contributing to decreased patient access,” Emond said. “While the U.S. has produced some of the world’s most incredible innovations, patients are still experiencing significant barriers to care. Now more than ever, it is crucial that we start working towards the goal of pairing fair pricing with fair access—leading to a more affordable health system for us all.”

Posthoc analyses in women divided by menopausal status show how Novo’s next-generation GLP-1 drug affects key cohorts of patients.
Novo has reported 25% weight loss in women taking CagriSema, largely replicating data on Eli Lilly’s rival drug in post hoc analyses that subdivided patients by menopausal status.
Multiple studies have found that women lose more weight than men on GLP-1 receptor agonists. Novo’s post hoc analysis of REDEFINE 1, a Phase 3 trial in adults with obesity or overweight, added to the evidence. Having reported 22.7% weight loss after 68 weeks in the overall population, Novo this week revealed that women in the trial who took the injectable medicine lost 25% of their body weight over the same period.
Novo shared the analysis at The Menopause Society 2026 Annual Meeting in San Diego. The analysis, which included 2,309 women, assumed all patients adhered to treatment. Participants on placebo lost 3% of their body weight.
The Danish drugmaker presented a second analysis of 1,902 women based on their stage of menopause, which is associated with obesity. Average weight loss was highest in premenopausal women, who shed 26.7% of their body weight by week 68. Average weight loss in peri- and postmenopausal women was 24.8% and 23.1%, respectively. Weight loss on placebo in the three subgroups ranged from 1.7% to 2.6%.
Obesity
Should amylin have been obesity therapeutics’ primary target from the start?
While GLP-1 medicines have become synonymous with weight loss, at least one expert thinks amylin would have been the go-to target if biopharma had been focused on the blockbuster indication 10 years ago. A new wave of therapies is now exploring this potentially gentler mechanism.
October 19, 2026
·
5 min read
·
Heather McKenzie
Read more
Novo’s findings echo data on tirzepatide, the GLP-1/GIP receptor agonist that Lilly sells as Mounjaro for diabetes and Zepbound for weight loss. In 2024, Lilly reported that women enrolled in its SURMOUNT clinical trials lost up to 24.6% of their body weight, compared to up to 18.1% for their male counterparts.
A subsequent analysis looked at weight loss by menopausal stage in two of the SURMOUNT trials. At week 72 of SURMOUNT-3, Lilly reported weight loss in pre-, peri- and postmenopausal women of 25.5%, 24.4% and 21.5%, respectively. Lilly saw weight loss of 29.4% in pre- and perimenopausal women in SURMOUNT-4, although that was a week 88 analysis. Weight loss typically increases over time.
In June, Lilly shared week 72 data on Foundayo, its oral GLP-1 drug, in peri- and postmenopausal women. Weight loss was lower on Foundayo than on CagriSema, peaking at 14.4% in perimenopausal women. The finding is in line with results showing that oral GLP-1s deliver lower weight loss than injectables in general.
Lilly’s retatrutide could be CagriSema’s most direct competitor, with both drug candidates nearing FDA approval and achieving deeper weight loss than existing GLP-1 receptor agonists in clinical trials. Lilly has yet to share analyses of retatrutide’s effects by menopausal stage.

Photo: Sri Lanka Ports Authority
By Angelo Mathais India correspondent
21 October 2026
Global terminal operators, backed by container shipping groups, are keenly eyeing fresh concessions at Sri Lanka’s Colombo port, according to industry sources.
One opportunity up for grabs soon is a rebid for South Asia Gateway Terminals (SAGT), where 30-year concession rights end in 2029.
SAGT’s ownership has four partners: 42% held by John Keells Holdings; 33% by Maersk/APMT; 15% by Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA); and 10% by Evergreen.
According to sources in Colombo, Sri Lankan policymakers are not considering a further extension of the concession term but will seek new proposals.
“There are clear signals that SLPA will go in for a fresh tendering attempt,” one source told The Loadstar .
SAGT, which has three berths with a total quay of 940 metres, and able to handle 2m teu annually, began operations in 1999. The terminal handled 1.8m teu in fiscal year 2025-26, which was down 11% year on year, as the Middle East crisis resulted in a wave of service suspensions, according to available data.
Sources said most major liners were upbeat about staking a claim for SAGT, with indications that Maersk will partner with another European liner to jointly pursue the concession rights.
The Danish group had previously explored collaborating with an Asian carrier, but the prospect of EU regulatory clearance risks was understood to have derailed that move, sources added.
“A joint bid between two European liner behemoths could be a game-changer for Colombo’s terminal operations,” one Sri Lankan port veteran told The Loadstar .
Sources believe Colombo’s booming transhipment traffic offers investors a stronger growth proposition, so bidding for any upcoming projects at the port is expected to be heated.
Despite the nagging capacity strain and growing competition from Indian ports, Colombo saw combined throughput in H1 26 spike 12% year on year, to 4.4m teu.
Meanwhile, until new concessions emerge or become operational, Adani Group’s $750m investment in Colombo West International Terminal (CWIT) is seen to be Colombo’s primary growth engine.
CWIT has officially launched phase 2 operations, doubling its capacity to 3.2m teu, after hitting 2m teu within 18 months of phase 1 operations, claimed to be the fastest growth seen by any operator at the port.
“With additional capacity, CWIT would be able to simultaneously berth three ultra-large container vessels, strengthening Colombo’s position as a critical transhipment hub on the east-west trade route,” said Adani Ports (APSEZ).
“Phase 2 is a landmark for APSEZ’s international portfolio and sharpens our position across the Indian Ocean’s key trade corridors. With expanded capacity, full automation and deepwater infrastructure, CWIT is built to be Colombo’s premier transshipment gateway and contribute to export/import cargo in Sri Lanka.”
In recent years, Adani has markedly expanded its terminal networks beyond India, aiming to become the world’s largest port operator handling 1bn tonnes of cargo across markets by 2030 – doubling the 500m tonnes in fiscal 2025-26.

Hibsago’s approval—a functional cure for certain patients with a hepatitis B infection—further validates Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ antisense platform, which has already generated two other new drug approvals this year.
The FDA has given the go-ahead to GSK and Ionis Pharmaceuticals’ antisense oligonucleotide bepirovirsen for the treatment of chronic hepatitis B virus infection, giving some patients the chance to potentially get off long-term medication.
Bepiroversen, to be marketed under the brand name Hibsago, can help patients achieve undetectable levels of the virus in the blood after six months—serving as a functional cure, according to GSK’s announcement on Tuesday.
GSK has forecasted peak worldwide sales of over £2 billion ($2.67 billion) for the drug, Reuters reported in May. BMO Capital Markets was more conservative in their estimate, projecting peak risk-unadjusted sales of $659 million in a Tuesday afternoon investor note.
Ionis will receive 10–12% tiered royalties on GSK’s sales—about $163 million, by BMO’s estimate—a “relatively modest” contribution to the company’s commercial business, the analysts wrote. But the approval “adds meaningful validation” of Ionis’ antisense oligonucleotide (ASO) platform after recent setbacks to the overall class, BMO continued. The firm pointed to the Phase 3 failure of Ionis’ AstraZeneca-partnered ASO Wainua in transthyretin-mediated amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) this summer and the September miss of Ultragenyx’s investigational ASO in Angelman syndrome.
Rare diseases
Ionis Paves Its Own Path as Initial Tryngolza Launch Defies Expectations
Long an R&D company that partnered off assets, RNAi biotech Ionis Pharmaceuticals shifted in 2025 to bring two medicines to market alone. Analysts are already impressed—and there’s more to come in 2026.
February 18, 2026
·
3 min read
·

Read more
Hibsago marks Ionis’ third ASO approval this year, following the September victory of Zanvastro for Alexander disease and the June clearance of Tryngolza to lower blood lipid levels and pancreatitis risk in patients with severe hypertriglyceridemia.
“While [Hibsago’s] approval was generally anticipated, we view this as another indication of the capabilities for the ASO platform Ionis has built,” BMO wrote.
Hibsago is given via subcutaneous injection every six months, and patients have the option to self-administer the drug after the first dose. It is indicated for use in combination with nucleos(t)ide analog reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTI) and is approved for adult patients who have no liver scarring, according to GSK.
Patients must have also been on NRTI treatment for at least six months and meet certain biomarker thresholds, as determined by an FDA-approved test.
Alongside Hibsago’s approval, the agency cleared Roche’s Elecsys HBsAg II quant II RxDx assay as a diagnostic device to identify patients with chronic hepatitis B who are eligible for treatment. The assay is also meant to help monitor patients while undergoing treatment.
Originally developed by Ionis, Hibsago was licensed by GSK in August 2019 with $25 million upfront plus up to $262 million in milestones. The antisense therapy targets the genetic material of the hepatitis B virus and tags it for destruction. This mechanism prevents the virus’ replication, while also boosting the immune system’s capabilities to fight off the infection. The FDA previously granted Hibsago breakthrough and priority review designations.
Hibsago’s approval was supported by data from the Phase 3 B-Well studies. The program consists of two late-stage studies, B-Well 1 and B-Well 2 , which together enrolled more than 1,800 adults with chronic hepatitis B who had been exposed to NRTI treatment. Participants were given either Hibsago or placebo. Both trials primarily assessed for functional cure, defined as having no detectable levels of the virus for 24 weeks after ending all hepatitis B medication.
Infectious disease
GSK, Ionis’ hepatitis B functional cure effectively eliminates virus in nearly 20% of patients
The antisense oligonucleotide was even more effective in patients with relatively low viral activity. More than one-quarter of these individuals had undetectable levels of the virus in the blood for at least six months after stopping treatment.
May 28, 2026
·
2 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
Detailed findings from the B-Well studies presented in May showed that Hibsago resulted in a 19% functional cure response rate. None of the patients on placebo hit functional cure.
In a key secondary analysis, GSK focused on patients with low baseline levels of the virus’ surface antigen. Hibsago treatment elicited a 26% functional cure rate in this subgroup, the pharma said on Tuesday.
“Hibsago provides a new treatment approach that gives some patients the possibility of maintaining control of the virus after all chronic HBV treatment has ended,” Wendy Carter, acting director of the FDA’s Office of Infectious Diseases under the Center for Drugs of Evaluation and Research, said in an agency release . “This approval represents an important advance for people living with this serious disease.”
As for safety, the FDA added a boxed warning on the Hibsago logo warning of serious liver reactions and low platelet counts, which the regulator said could aggravate the likelihood of potentially life-threatening bleeding. Other warnings for the drug include serious inflammatory side effects and declining kidney function.

Australian Army and Indonesian Armed Forces Engineers conduct urban clearance training during Exercise Keris Woomera 26 at Pusat Latihan Pertempuran Marinir 5, Indonesia. (Photo: Australian Department of Defence)
SINGAPORE — Australia and Indonesia have concluded a bilatera l defense exercise that involved thousands of personnel and included a number of “firsts” for Canberra — the latest in what an analyst said were a series of trust-building and integration exercises between the nations.
Exercise Keris Woomera took place between 12 and 20 October in and around the eastern part of Indonesia’s most populous island of Java, and saw approximately 1,000 Australian personnel take part alongside their Indonesian counterparts. The Australian Department of Defence called Keris Woomera “the largest overseas training activity for the Australian Defence Force (ADF) for the year.”
“The exercise e nables the Tentara Nasional Indonesia (TNI) to conduct high-end joint training with the ADF [Australian Defence Force], contributing to their own capacity to deter military coercion and defend Indonesian sovereignty,” the ADF said on its website .
It added that the exercise would “ensure ADF can deter a potential adversary’s attempts to project power against Australia, and be prepared to protect Australia and its maritime approaches.”
The ADF said the exercise played host to several firsts, including the “first time the high mobility artillery rocket system (HIMARS) deployed and fired overseas, the first deployment of a RAAF 4 Squadron aircraft into South-East Asia since World War II and the first time Australia conducted cyber integration training with Indonesia.”
“By operating side-by-side, this year’s iteration has shown how Australia and Indonesia can integrate to address shared security challenges and positively impact how we respond to a rapidly evolving strategic environment.
‘Increasingly Frequent Exercises’
The exercise comes just months after both countries signed the Australia-Indonesia Treaty on Common Security in February which, among other things, reaffirms the relationship between both countries and a desire “to contribute to regional security and stability”
Fauzan Malufti, a researcher at the Jakarta-based Ce ntre for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS), said that “Keris Woomera is part of a wider series of increasingly frequent exercises between the TNI and ADF, which will help build trust and familiarity at both the unit and leadership levels.”
He told Breaking Defense that the exercis e was expected to be confidence building for both sides and improve the interoperability.
“The exercise helps TNI and ADF better understand each other’s procedures, communications, planning, and command systems so they can operate together better, especially in combat scenarios,” he added.
This year’s iteration of the exercise was the second in the series since the inaugural event in 2024, and Malufti said he believes that the Australians would like to see the exercise scale up in complexity as the regional security situation becomes more “challenging.”
He pointed out that Indonesia’s capabilities and other political considerations might nevertheless see it reluctant to widen the scope of future exercises, noting that Indonesia’s commitment to non-alignment might result in it not wanting to be seen as leaning towards any particular country.
“TNI capacity is another factor, as engagement with other foreign militaries is also increasing, while the TNI’s growing involvement in domestic non-defense activities continues to consume a huge number of resources and leadership attention”, he said.
Australia’s involvement in Keris Woomera comes amidst a busy October for its interactions with regional militaries. A detachment of its Lockheed Martin F-35 Lighting II fifth-generation fighters are currently deployed to Singapore as part of a contingent taking part in the Five Power Defence Arrangements exercis e called Bersama Lima together with the militaries of Malaysia, New Zealand, Singapore and the United Kingdom.
Another 300-strong contingent from the ADF is also currently in Japan participating in Exercise Keen Sword , where it is sending a frigate and a Boeing P-8A Poseidon multi-mission anti-submarine aircraft alongside the forces of Japan, the US and six other nations

Cargo thieves have learned to work the space between a broker and a carrier. They impersonate carriers, intercept load data and redirect shipments. Michael Caney, chief commercial officer of Highway, says no single vendor can close those gaps, and that freight needs shared standards for the data brokers use to choose carriers.
Highway sells carrier identity and vetting tools to freight brokers, and Caney has described it as the Plaid for freight . He said Highway answers to the 1,500 brokers that pay it to manage risk, and that its customer base and integrations give it more data than anyone on who is moving North American truckload freight and how likely each load is to be stolen.
That data backs a performance guarantee. If a broker follows Highway’s recommendations and the load is stolen anyway, Highway pays $100,000. Caney said Highway has covered a million loads under the guarantee and lost one .
Highway walked customers through the guarantee at its Aug. 31 to Sept. 2 user summit in Frisco, Texas. The other topic was an expansion of what Highway calls its shared accountability model.
The model starts from who touches a load. For years, Caney said, he thought a load had two parties, the broker and the carrier. He now counts five. The other three are the insurance agent and insurer, the factoring company and the telematics provider.
“All of these parties provide data and introduce risk, yet none is accountable when a theft occurs,” Caney said in an interview with FreightWaves. “There’s no incentive alignment.”
Gaps in insurance and factoring data
In insurance, a carrier takes a truck off its scheduled auto policy, and the change never makes it from the insurer to the agent to Highway. The broker learns the truck isn’t covered after an accident or cargo damage.
“How many insurance agents have come forward and said, ‘I’m sorry. That’s on me. Let me help you, Mr. Freight Broker’?” Caney said. “Zero.”
Many factoring companies, which buy carriers’ freight bills, care only whether the broker on the other end will pay.
“As long as the debtor is creditworthy and the factoring company can collect what it’s owed, it has little incentive to care if its customer steals freight. There’s no accountability,” he said.
Providers that vouch for their data
Highway’s answer is a certified network of providers that agree to stand behind their data. The first phase, Highway Certified Insurance Agencies, launched June 1 with 10 founding agencies . They commit to accurate certificates of insurance, coverage detail down to the VIN and timely notice of policy changes, cancellations and nonrenewals. Highway plans to extend the certification to other service providers in brokered freight.
Customers asked Highway to build the network, Caney said. The data reaching brokers had accuracy problems, he added, including bad policy dates and VIN data.
Caney argued in an Oct. 7 FreightWaves commentary that ELD data needs an enforceable standard too, and that Highway sets integration requirements beyond FMCSA registration.
“There are FMCSA-certified ELD providers that we won’t integrate with,” Caney said.
The certification pitch split the providers Highway approached.
“We heard from people who said, ‘This is exactly what the industry needs. I’m tired of competing against those who cut corners,’'” he said. “But not everyone welcomed that level of accountability.”
Fraud moves from rules to process
The push for standards follows where fraud has gone. Caney said social engineering is now a major threat, including voice AI used to call brokers and ask them to send load information to a new email address or by text.
“What is happening with fraud is a direct attack on process,” he said. “It’s no longer just about a set of rules.”
Caney calls fraud a choice. Highway tells brokers that emailing a rate confirmation as an attachment makes a stolen load very likely. A carrier with a limited-term CDL won’t necessarily steal the load, he said, but the broker has to take two or three more steps to make sure.
The trouble sits in a narrow slice of the market. More than 82% of the carriers that move brokered freight qualify for the performance guarantee, Highway told FreightWaves in September. In most broker networks, Caney said, 6% of carriers are ones brokers shouldn’t be talking to, and some brokers load them anyway.
“If you’re shopping on the day-old bread aisle, you shouldn’t be surprised when the bread is stale” he said.
Loads on that 6% fall outside the guarantee.
Accountability after Montgomery
The stakes for brokers rose in May, when the Supreme Court ruled unanimously in Montgomery v. Caribe Transport II that brokers can face state negligent-hiring claims over the carriers they select.
Brokers should be wary of anyone who claims to have the answer, Caney said, himself included.
“You’re dealing with people’s livelihoods, including the broker’s. After Montgomery, that’s a serious responsibility,” he said.
Caney points to Visa in payments and the Buttonwood Agreement among early stock traders as the kind of standards freight never set. The industry won’t change, he said, until every participant plays by the same rules.
“We have to come together and agree on some ground rules if we want to be part of the rising tide that lifts all boats,'” Caney said. “Highway is trying to help set and steward those standards, but the industry has to decide what it’s willing to tolerate.”

Volkswagen's Steering Rack Bolt Recall Includes 239,202 Atlas and Tiguan Sport Utility Vehicles
26 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
While road salt may be great for keeping winter roads drivable, sodium chloride and moisture are a terrible cocktail for a bunch of stuff underneath your car. The Volkswagen Group knows it all too well due to a bolt that secures the steering rack to the front subframe, namely a bolt that can prematurely corrode from salt and water exposure.
The worldwide recall now numbers more than four million vehicles, of which the Atlas and Tiguan are listed with 239,202 units by the Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt. As per Germany's Federal Motor Transport Authority, the subject bolt can easily break, leaving the driver without steering control. The KBA presently monitors the problem under campaign number 17124R.
As far as the Atlas people mover and Tiguan crossover are concerned, suspect vehicles were produced between November 28, 2016, and September 22, 2018. The Volkswagen Group calls this campaign 48VT, and the KBA lists precisely 454 affected vehicles in the German market.
As noted earlier, corrosion is the biggest problem here. Over time, road salt exposure and other environmental factors can rust the steering rack mounting bolt so much that a failure cannot be ruled out. When it breaks, the steering rack's housing can also fracture, leading to a loss of steering control at high speed.
Volkswagen's US subsidiary describes the same failure mode for the US market, and the recall filing published by the NHTSA reveals that a replacement bolt with better corrosion resistance is on the menu. The Wolfsburg-based automaker claims the new part uses a polymer coating designed specifically to keep salt and moisture away from the fastener.
Photo: Volkswagen The question is, was this a supplier issue or simply Volkswagen opting for a cheaper part to save production costs? While that question may not have an answer right now, it doesn't change the fact that over four million cars and sport utility vehicles are being recalled across the world.
In the US, campaign 26V590 also includes a bunch of 2019 through 2021 model year Audi Q3 vehicles. Said campaign uses 48VT for the Volkswagen side of the recall and 48LG for the Audi side. In both cases, owner notification letters are scheduled for November 2026.
The KBA's campaign is both narrower and broader at the same time. Not only does it cover more vehicles than the US campaign, but it doesn't include the Audi Q3. Regardless, the recall includes MQB-based vehicles exclusively. The group found this problem through multiple investigations into steering rack bolt corrosion reports across multiple nameplates.
Volkswagen hasn't announced a completion date for the repairs beyond the notification schedule, which is only natural when you remember how many replacement bolts are required worldwide. That said, both the Atlas and the Tiguan are the most popular Volkswagen crossovers in the US market.
Per the Q3 2026 sales release from Volkswagen of America, the Tiguan leads with 28,091 deliveries for the quarter. The Atlas and Atlas Cross Sport moved 15,375 and 6,889 units during the analyzed three-month period.

Dreamstime
By Alexander Whiteman
21 October 2026
African airfreight is seeing something of a boom from the disruption in ocean freight across the Middle East, but forwarders remain sceptical as to whether it will provoke long-term structural benefits.
Hennie Heymans, CEO of DHL Express’s Sub-Saharan Africa operations, told The Loadstar the shift from ocean services had left airfreight the only viable alternative to keep goods moving.
“When people run into trouble from a seafreight point of view, the alternative becomes airfreight, becomes express, and that is a notable trend across African airfreight’s growth momentum at the moment,” Mr Heymans told The Loadstar .
For DHL Express, the timing has proved particularly useful, coinciding with the launch of its Heavy Weight Express service, allowing its customers to ship consignments of up to 3,000kg, with individual pieces of up to 1,000kg.
Expanding beyond smaller parcels, the new service is designed for automotive, energy, engineering, machinery, and pharmaceuticals, Mr Heymans noting the significant cost implications delays place on these sectors.
“The timing of the launch worked out quite well, which makes the conversation a lot easier, and a lot more comfortable for those customers seeking these sorts of services,” explained Mr Heymans.
However, he did not disclose how much additional volume DHL Express had gained as a result of shipping disruption, nor how much of the growth in airfreight was a result of transference from ocean freight over underlying growth patterns.
Anecdotal evidence from forwarders active on the African west and south coasts indicates that the continent is experiencing an uptick in demand for capacity, with overall volumes growing, but none was able to tell The Loadstar how the present situation should be assessed.
One forwarder said: “There’s definite growth in demand for capacity in and out of certain countries around the continent – Nigeria, South Africa, and Ghana are big lanes for us – but if it is specific modes, we can only say that uptick in airfreight bookings is transference.”
Others believe there are long-term prospects on the airfreight side for the continent’s major players, with forwarders noting that the chaos in the Middle East, issues with the US, and looming threats in Asia were leading all to reconsider their supply chain make-up.

2027 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 Truck Production Underway at Silao Factory in Mexico
33 photos
Photo: Chevrolet
The Silao assembly complex in Mexico spent four weeks down before 2027 model year Silverado half-ton pickups started rolling off the line. General Motors big kahuna Mary Barra and chief financial officer Paul Jacobson confirmed the news to investors during the Q3 2026 earnings call, adding that US dealers will get 2027s in the latter part of the fourth quarter.
Production at Fort Wayne and Orion is planned to start in 2027. As per Jacobson, production at Silao began at a measured pace. It will build towards normal output levels over the following months, which means that supply could be limited in the first half of the 2027 model year. Getting the line running properly before running it flat out is the less glamorous part of launching a new pickup, that's for sure!
The vehicle assembly complex in Fort Wayne, Indiana, should get its turn after some downtime beginning in December 2026, with 2027 Silverado 1500 production scheduled to start in January 2027. The Orion Township facility in Michigan will also build Silverado half-ton pickups, with Barra targeting the second quarter of 2027.
Of course, the mechanically similar 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 shares the rollout. Beyond these facilities, General Motors allocated Silverado 1500 and Sierra 1500 engine production to a bunch of North American plants. Flint Engine Operations, for example, handles the 3.0-liter Duramax turbo diesel inline-six and small blocks.
The 5.7- and 6.6-liter V8 engines that replace the old 5.3- and 6.2-liter units also come from Tonawanda Propulsion and St. Catharines Propulsion. The final piece of the puzzle is the 2.7-liter TurboMax, a four-pot turbo gasser that is made in Spring Hill, Tennessee.
All 10-speed trannies are produced at the Romulus and Toledo plants in Michigan and Ohio. While final assembly occurs there, Bedford Casting Operations specializes in aluminum die-cast transmission cases, including cases meant for the 10L boxes used by the redesigned trucks.
Photo: General Motors Speaking to investors, Barra made it clear that General Motors focused on the stuff truck customers desire most in half-ton pickups. Think usable torque, predictable delivery, trailering and durability under load, as well as real-world fuel consumption. To ensure all that, Barra revealed that gen-six V8 small blocks had accumulated more than 100,000 hours on the dyno and over 1.6 million validation miles (or 2.6 million kilometers in metric speak).
Although the 5.7- and 6.6-liter small blocks are the most anticipated engines for 2027, the Duramax soldiers on as one of the most interesting engines in the half-ton segment. Not only does it make the Silverado 1500 and Sierra 1500 unique in the segment, but over 900 miles (1,448 kilometers) of highway range is huge.
Said highway mileage when the diesel is optioned is only possible with the 34-gallon (129-liter) fuel tank. As far as Chevrolet is concerned, the shopping language has also changed for the 2027 model year. Instead of the LT, the Silverado 1500's middle trim level is referred to as the Silverado in advertising materials and media releases. That, however, is a bit misleading.
Firing up the 2027 model's configurator, the midgrade is actually called LT when specified with rear-wheel drive or Z71 with four-wheel drive. Considering that Z71 goodies come standard when optioning four-wheel drive, it sure makes sense to call it as such. Barra also described how the High Country is moving closer to the materials, tech, and features you would normally associate with luxury SUVs.
Super Cruise becomes standard on high-end grades, with optional availability on lesser grades. Both the Silverado 1500 and Sierra 1500 support hands-free driving with trailering across more than 630,000 miles (over 1 million clicks) of compatible North American roads, especially highways.

This 1970 Pontiac Has the Perfect Package: All-Original Survivor, in a Garage Since Day One
14 photos
Photo: eBay seller risingsunset
While 1970 was in some ways the beginning of the end for the GTO, this Catalina is here to remind us that Pontiac was still fine that year. This car is advertised as an all-original survivor, and the reason it’s online is simple: it needs a loving home where it can get the minor TLC it needs.
This isn’t a restored or molested car. It’s a specimen that has always been babied, and the seller claims that this Pontiac never slept outside. It has always been parked inside since day one, which kind of explains its condition.
The owner says the Catalina “needs absolutely nothing,” but I don’t think this is entirely true. It does need a few occasional touches, especially if your objective is to park the car in a collection. Just open the trunk to see what I mean.
There’s obvious surface rust, but there’s nothing too dramatic or something that could make people walk away. It’s minor corrosion that hasn’t gotten through, so my recommendation is that you call the seller and arrange an in-person inspection before you even make an offer. This Catalina isn’t supposed to be a car that you drive every day, so yes, you must make sure that it checks all the right boxes.
Photo: eBay seller risingsunset The Catalina went through lots of changes in the second half of the ‘60s, including the demise of the 2+2 in 1968 and the introduction of larger and larger grilles. While 1970 models aren’t exactly rare - if you want a rare Catalina, you should look for a last-year 2+2, as Pontiac produced only 1,768 coupes and convertibles in 1967- they are still highly desirable, particularly thanks to their design.
Pontiac itself bragged about the redesigned Catalina in 1970.
“Face it, folks. The 1970 Catalina is all wrong. For the money, you should get a so-so-sized car with hee-haw styling and a ho-hum interior. But, no. Catalina is big, big, big. Lots of room for legs and heads,” Pontiac said before moving its attention to engines and styling. The grille was the thing that caught everybody’s attention.
“The styling - Catalina’s strength. That incredible new grille is strictly top-of-the-line,” Pontiac said.
The GM brand used every occasion to recommend that buyers pay extra for the Ventura package, which brought carpeted lower door panels, new seats with extra padding, a perforated taffeta headliner, and special trim inside and out.
Photo: eBay seller risingsunset The Catalina sedan was standard with a 350ci engine rated at 255 horsepower, while the rest of the versions were fitted with a 400ci unit with 290 horsepower. Pontiac offered not one, not two, but five optional engines at a time when the American car space was moving towards more efficient and smaller engines.
The optional engine list started with a 400ci unit with 265 horsepower and went all the way up to 455 cubic inches and 370 horsepower.
This Catalina has a 400 under the hood, but that’s where the available information ends. No further specifics were shared, but considering it’s an all-original survivor, this should be the factory-installed unit.
It should be in tip-top shape already, considering the owner says you can drive the Pontiac home. However, I would still ask my mechanic to inspect it thoroughly, especially considering the survivor promise, which implies that the engine has never been rebuilt.
Photo: eBay seller risingsunset Otherwise, an in-person inspection is the one that should help figure out the full story. The paint has lost its shine, and the interior faces some discoloration, which makes perfect sense, considering the car has never been refreshed.
The trunk rust makes me wonder if the floors are clean, so if you go there in person, make sure you raise this Pontiac on a lift to inspect the underside. The vehicle shouldn’t come with any patches, considering it’s an all-original specimen, and the seller insists on the “no major rust anywhere” claim.
Overall, I do think that this Catalina will find a home eventually, but I don’t think it’ll happen without further specifics and maybe a walkaround video to help bidders figure out what they’re buying.
Photo: eBay seller risingsunset The owner looks committed to letting the car go, as they posted this Pontiac for auction on eBay without a reserve. This allows the top bidder to take the Pontiac home when the battle ends, though if someone wants to get their hands on it without a fight, they can just trigger the Buy It Now option and pay $10,000.
Otherwise, you can bid against others for the car, and the starting bid is $5,000. So far, the auction hasn’t received any bids, but this isn’t necessarily surprising for a no-reserve auction, as many bidders might be waiting until the last minute to submit an offer to avoid a fierce battle.
The vehicle is parked in Scranton, Pennsylvania, and remember that the auction ends in just 3 days, so you might be running out of time to call the seller and ask your questions.

CSX has eliminated 109 operations management positions as part of a restructuring of its engineering functions.
The organizational changes were first outlined this past spring, a CSX (NASDAQ: CSX ) spokesman said in an email to FreightWaves. The cuts “are intended to establish a more effective operating structure and better align field support with the needs of the railroad, while maintaining the capabilities necessary to safely operate and maintain the network and serve our customers.”
Headquartered in Jacksonville, CSX in January CSX laid off 166 management employees, or about 5% of the non-union workforce at the time.
CSX is releasing third quarter earnings today after the close of markets. Zacks consensus estimate expects revenue of $3.96 billion, up about 10.3% year over year. Earnings per share of $0.53 is up about 20.5% from last year’s adjusted $0.44.
The spokesman said 58 affected employees were offered new roles within operations and 51 were offered severance. Of those offered severance, 75% have union seniority and may return to craft positions, including roles in areas where CSX continues to have vacancies across the network.
“We recognize the impact these decisions have on our colleagues and their families, and CSX is supporting affected employees through the transition,” the spokesman said.
The job cuts come as CSX Chief Operating Officer Mike Cory announced his retirement. His duties are being reassigned to two current executives.

source_document.body:
Customers expect a Managed Transportation partner to run their freight reliably and cost efficiently. They should get more: experts who understand their network, bring ideas for making it better, and drive those changes. The scale and knowledge of their partner should work to their advantage.
At Uber Freight, we call this Transportation Orchestration and it’s the next step in delivering on this promise. It means continuously monitoring how customers’ networks perform, identifying opportunities to improve, and increasingly automating the decisions and execution that turn those insights into results. Our scale creates opportunities to improve each customer’s network in ways no individual company could achieve alone.
Advances in AI expand what is possible. Even the best experts can only review so much information at once. AI enables us to analyze far more network data in real time, identify better options, and increasingly automate action. As routine execution becomes more automated, our experts can focus more on advising customers and implementing strategic changes. Those changes—and their results—feed back into the system, improving future recommendations and helping us identify where similar improvements could benefit other customers.
As Chief Product Officer, my focus is on building that loop so our capabilities and expertise grow more powerful with every interaction.
A partner that sees what’s next
In my first few months at Uber Freight, customer conversations have sharpened my thinking about the opportunity ahead. Running today’s freight well is essential table stakes. Customers benefit the most when we bring ideas and drive the change tomorrow requires.
Customers value visibility and expect us to act on it: anticipate disruptions, protect service, and address recurring problems at the source. When demand, freight rates, or facility operations change, they need guidance on the implications for service and budgets—and help executing the right response.
As a partner working across shippers in a broad range of industries, we bring a broad perspective, helping customers understand what is possible and which changes are worth pursuing.
Making the next decision smarter
We see three connected steps toward increasingly autonomous network planning and freight execution: automate routine work, turn data into actionable intelligence, and increasingly automate execution.
First, automation makes planning, tracking, and information gathering faster and more consistent, with fewer errors. Second, intelligence helps identify patterns, diagnose problems, and recommend better options. Third, we connect that intelligence to tools that turn recommendations to action, with experts remaining in the loop to guide high judgment decisions. We capture and measure the results, feeding them back into the system to deepen the system’s transportation knowledge and improve future decisions.
For example, repeated late deliveries might reveal that a route consistently takes longer than planned. The system identifies the pattern, adjusts the plan within agreed parameters, and measures whether service improves. No digging through reports, analyzing data, or manual decision and action taking needed. If it works, that learning helps identify similar issues in other customers’ networks—so one improvement becomes the starting point for others.
Make the broader network work for each customer
Some improvements come from understanding one customer’s operations deeply. Others require looking across shippers.
For years, the industry has largely optimized within individual networks. A private fleet may be well planned around one shipper’s freight, while two shippers may each have a workable plan that leaves their trucks partially filled—even when their shipments could move together. Improvements happen incrementally at the edges where opportunities arise, often leaving carriers to connect the pieces across networks.
Looking across those networks creates a bigger opportunity: coordinating freight and capacity to lower costs in ways individual shippers cannot achieve alone. Finding those opportunities requires understanding each shipper’s constraints; delivering them requires coordinated execution.
Uber Freight brings together the network insight and capabilities to orchestrate that execution. Managing our customers’ logistics gives us operational expertise, our marketplace connects us to capacity, and Uber provides a technology foundation we are building upon. Our product priority is to make these opportunities easier to identify, evaluate, and execute consistently, so more customers benefit from our scale.
AI empowers experts to drive change
Our logistics experts understand the constraints and trade-offs that determine whether a recommendation will work in the real world. Their judgment remains essential as agents take on more routine execution.
With more data and analysis at their fingertips, our experts can bring customers better ideas, guide network decisions, and implement strategic changes. Customers should feel that shift in the partnership: technology handling more daily execution, with experts focused on what their network needs next.
The vision is ambitious. Progress has to be tangible.
Transportation Orchestration is the future we’re building toward. We are moving with urgency: improving the data that informs recommendations, connecting those recommendations to execution, and proving that agentic execution delivers tangible benefits and reliable results in customers’ operations. We are iterating on these capabilities, learning as we go, and expanding what works across all the freight we manage. This will take time to build, but every step will create value.
Customers will judge our progress through the outcomes that matter to their business: lower costs, reliable service, and faster adaptation as their businesses change. Our responsibility is to deliver networks that continuously get better—with systems that operate autonomously and experts guiding high-judgment decisions to drive strategic change.
Let’s build!
— Amir Pelleg, Chief Product Officer, Uber Freight

Japan's Toyota Upgrade Factory Rolls Out Land Cruiser VX Round Headlight Conversion
11 photos
Photo: Toyota
Toyota is now obliged to help Land Cruiser VX owners in Japan change their minds about the design of the headlights. Offered through Toyota Upgrade Factory, a retrofit service operated by KINTO, the round headlamp conversion is advertised in the Land of the Rising Sun at 204,600 yen. That's 1,300 dollars at press time, including tax and labor.
Giving the 250-series Land Cruiser a more traditional face, said headlights aren't easy to install. Dealers must remove and reinstall the front bumper. As part of the process, a control unit has to be reprogrammed as well, just as expected from a headlight upgrade on a tech-infused vehicle. Speaking of which, the VX grade of the Land Cruiser 250 presently retails at 5,779,400 yen (36,560 dollars).
Switching from rectangular to round headlights makes a world of difference, while packaging the hardware and installation together ensures proper operation. Round lights perfectly suit the broad and upright front end of the 250 series, which is also called Prado in certain markets, because they interrupt so much straight-edged bodywork with circular shapes.
A design you can easily associate with Land Cruisers from the good ol' days, the round lamps make a bigger difference to the 250's aesthetic than a strip of black exterior garnish and similar nonsense. According to Toyota Upgrade Factory, the newly launched circular headlights were designed for customers who feel drawn to the round lamps they saw in other markets.
Speaking of, the US-market Land Cruiser features both designs. Only available with five seats and four-pot turbo hybrid muscle, the American model uses round headlights for the 1958 trim level and rectangular headlights for the Land Cruiser trim level. Indeed, the iconic design is marketed as the cheaper option stateside.
Photo: Toyota Upgrade Factory Both designs use LED projectors and high-beam assistance, but they're not created equal. IIHS testing revealed the round headlights are superior in more scenarios, helping the 1958 grade secure the "good" rating for headlight performance as opposed to "marginal" for the rectangular units of the Land Cruiser grade.
Eligibility for Toyota Upgrade Factory's round headlights includes VX models produced from April 2024 through March 2026, plus those following the April 2026 partial update. In addition to old-school headlights packing modern tech, Toyota Upgrade Factory has also rolled out the Gen5 wireless phone charger.
Priced at 28,600 yen fitted, which is merely 180 bucks at current exchange rates, the new charging pad is a Land Cruiser 250-specific unit. Compared to the previous unit, Gen5 doubles the charging area, thus addressing the problem of phones shifting away from the position where wireless charging actually works.
The larger charging area reduces interruptions caused by movement while driving, and phones are likely to move a lot in a body-on-frame SUV that can hold its own in off-road scenarios. The Gen5 charger supports fast charging, with performance depending on the phone's hardware. The lights and charger join a broader Toyota Upgrade Factory retrofit menu, which includes cargo area goodies, illuminated front scuff plates, and chunky mud flaps.
Searching through said catalog, the most interesting retrofit option is dubbed Shibetsu fins. That would be 20 small adhesive pieces that attach to the Land Cruiser VX's underside for improved driving stability. Each sheet-like fin is nearly 4 millimeters thick, 40 millimeters long, and 80 millimeters wide.
Via // Toyota Upgrade Factory

At a former flight-test base south of Paris, drones swoop over fields and woodland as teams on the ground test systems designed to stop them — a response to a growing wave of drone incursions and “hybrid attacks” since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022.
The potential clients for technology such as electronic jammers and interceptor drones tested at the Brétigny-sur-Orge site are no longer just governments, police and armies.
Private firms and state entities across Europe that operate critical infrastructure want to strengthen their defenses, with some utilities asking for authorization to shoot drones down themselves. From Paris to Berlin, governments are taking note.
They are worried that hybrid warfare or a drone attack could knock out power to millions of people — as has happened frequently in Ukraine after Russian strikes.
RELATED
Estonia weighs buying light jet aircraft to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones
Estonia's defense minister said the government should consider fielding aircraft capable of shooting down Russian jet-powered attack drones.
By Linus Höller
“It is a theoretical, and increasingly a practical, possibility that there could be heating outages this winter due to hybrid attacks,” Kristian Ruby, secretary general of European energy body Eurelectric, told Reuters.
Some European governments are responding by starting to give firms powers traditionally confined to the military. Interviews by Reuters with over 30 company executives, officials and drone experts meanwhile show the technology to detect and bring down drones is maturing faster than the rules on who may use it.
Approaches vary widely across Europe and legal uncertainties remain, including over who has the right to order a response to a drone threat. Bringing down a drone could cause injury or death to people on the ground or damage property, raising questions for companies about liability and accountability.
“Defenseless”
France is among countries that have led the way. Its parliament passed a law in August allowing approved operators of critical infrastructure and contractors to detect, jam and shoot down drones near designated facilities.
The law passed by the French parliament in August responded to a wave of drone incursions over critical and military sites, including flights over the Ile Longue nuclear submarine base near Brest in northwestern France in December 2025.
France wants a newly expanded list of sensitive sites deemed of vital importance equipped by 2027, a senior French official involved in the plans told Reuters, asking not to be named because details of the plan are not yet public.
“We were defenseless in the face of the (drone) threat,” the official said, adding that concerns had been growing over the last decade as unmanned aerial vehicles became more accessible and more common.
The French government wants to give operators of critical infrastructure such as state-owned utility company EDF and state-owned railway company SNCF a catalogue of approved systems ranging from electronic jammers to interceptor drones, depending on different environments and situations.
Confirming important elements of the plan outlined by the French official, Systematic Paris-Region, which runs the government testing program at Brétigny-sur-Orge, said evaluations launched this summer had so far catalogued three systems integrators — which combine different computer systems into a unified whole — and 17 counter-drone systems.
It said assessments were continuing and work was underway to accelerate procurement from among those solutions.
France’s defense ministry said the law passed in August would help strengthen capabilities to counter the threat, though it said it could speak only for the critical infrastructure under its authority. EDF and SNCF declined comment.
Who can bring down a drone?
The discovery of an explosives-laden drone near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Germany’s Leipzig/Halle airport in August underlined how far the risks have spread.
Germany blamed Russia for the incident. Moscow denied it was behind it, and has repeatedly denied carrying out hybrid attacks in Europe, many of which have been in countries that support Kyiv in Russia’s war in Ukraine.
But concerns are growing that national authorities cannot respond fast enough to protect widely dispersed infrastructure against such attacks, and that the damage caused by relatively cheap drones could bring hefty repair costs.
In Germany, where counter-drone operations remain a policing function, the interior ministry told Reuters it was reviewing how critical infrastructure operators and third parties could be legally involved in active counter-drone measures.
In September, Austria announced plans to give similar powers to critical infrastructure operators, including large energy firms. Defense Minister Klaudia Tanner told a press conference that the state could not protect every site on its own.
Poland has gone further. Operators told Reuters they have deployed counter-drone systems and trained with military and police units. Drone-restricted zones have been established around critical energy infrastructure, and designated security units working for operators have been authorized to destroy, disable or take control of drones entering them.
But two sources at energy transmission companies on NATO’s eastern flank told Reuters that effective intervention still requires more assurances, and perhaps a judicial precedent, on who bears responsibility for collateral damage.
Without that certainty, they said, operators of critical infrastructure could remain reluctant to neutralize drones because bringing one down could itself cause injury or costly damage.
Built for recovery
Having powers to bring down drones would be a change of approach for companies across Europe.
Executives, officials and energy analysts told Reuters that utilities have spent years hardening networks and preparing to restore disrupted services, rather than preventing attacks.
Leonhard Birnbaum, chief executive of German energy firm E.ON, said in September that operators must assume some attacks will succeed, rather than plan on stopping all of them. The company operates about 2,720 substations across Germany, he said.
Lithuania is building a fortified substation near its border with Russia as part of plans by the Baltic states and Poland to improve their defenses that include constructing bunkers , installing anti-drone nets and building up stocks of hard-to-replace equipment for critical parts of the energy grid.
Poland’s state-owned transmission operator PSE patrols parts of its about 16,500-km (10,250-mile) high-voltage network by helicopter and is preparing more powerful aircraft to help protect an undersea power link to Sweden.
Yet relatively inexpensive drones are challenging such defenses. Essential equipment such as large transformers can take years to replace, while even a successful repair can leave infrastructure out of service for months.
Not all utility operators are seeking a bigger role in defending themselves.
Asta Sihvonen-Punkka, chief executive of Finland’s national power grid operator Fingrid, told Reuters that responsibility for countering threats around critical infrastructure should remain with Finnish authorities and armed forces.
Any move to give such powers to utility operators would be “a very, very big change” requiring careful legal consideration, she said.
Jari Stenius, head of security of Finnish utility Fortum, said he was content for energy companies to focus on producing energy while police and military authorities handled security threats.
Technology ready, rules are not
Security officials and counter-drone technology firms say systems are becoming increasingly automated because operators cannot station specialist teams at every site.
Modern counter-drone systems combine sensors, command-and-control software and countermeasures into a single chain designed to identify, classify and respond to threats within seconds.
Several companies told Reuters that uncertainty over who can authorize a response has slowed investment in the latter stages of that process. France is therefore trying to automate the process as much as possible, said the senior French official involved in France’s plans.
The official said security workers at utilities should eventually be able to detect a threat and launch an automated response at the press of a button, because having operators trained to use military-grade solutions at every location was unrealistic.
German defense company Rheinmetall told Reuters the biggest hurdle for civilian operators was often the delay between detecting a drone and deciding whether to deploy a countermeasure, as legal responsibilities remain fragmented.
Rheinmetall said interest from private infrastructure operators in counter-drone systems was rising sharply.
The company said it was conducting workshops, site surveys and infrastructure assessments for operators and was preparing for what it described as a “very fast-growing” market segment.
(Reporting by Maria Rugamer and Leo Marchandon in Gdansk, Florence Loeve in Paris and Marek Strzelecki in Warsaw.)

By Gavin van Marle
21 October 2026
Air and sea freight volumes at the world’s largest freight forwarder, DSV, saw a decline in the third quarter, but revenues grew more than 15% year on year, due to elevated ocean freight rates.
According to third-quarter results released today, DSV posted group revenue of DKr71.9bn ($10.8bn), up 10.5% year on year, and an EBIT before special items of DKr5.4bn, up 19.5% year on year.
Its Air & Sea forwarding division reported a 3% decline in air freight tonnage and ocean freight teu, but a 15.9% increase in combined revenue, to DKr45.6bn, while EBIT before special items was up 19.8% year on year, to just under DKr4.3bn.
DSV also noted that over the first nine months of the year, its sea freight volumes had grown 13%, but attributed the Q3 decline to a mixture of “weaker commercial performance on the APAC-Europe tradelane and the effect of yield management initiatives.
It said: “The quarterly decline was greater than expected, but stabilised during the period.
“Performance was impacted by weak demand on Middle East-related tradelanes, where disruptions affected activity, while the APAC-Europe tradelane continued to be affected by integration-related commercial impacts in certain countries, particularly in Germany.”
Chief executive Jens Lund told analysts on DSV’s earnings call this morning the firm had spent the quarter “sanitising” its lower-paying and loss-making shipper accounts.
“I would say of the 3% decline, about two percentage points were sanitising and the remaining 1% a business decline, certainly in air freight,” he said.
Third-quarter air freight volumes also fell 3%, year on year, to 560,890 tonnes, although over the nine-month period they were up 15% year on year.
The company explained: “Despite a positive volume trend during the quarter, the decline was larger than expected.
“Volumes were impacted by yield-management initiatives, conversion from air freight to sea freight, lower-than expected activity in Europe and reduced e-commerce volumes on the APAC-Europe tradelane.
“This was partially offset by growth within the technology business in APAC and North America. Middle East-related tradelanes remained weak, due to the ongoing conflict in the region.”
Mr Lund added that between 20% and 25% of volumes were now running through the Tango TMS inherited through DSV’s acquisition of Schenker, the remainder being handled via the CargoWise system.
“It’s predominantly the larger clients that we have on that [Tango] platform – the more complex ones.
“We’ve not started any roll-out yet – we’ve said that we want to improve Tango, and it will also co-exist with CargoWise for quite a while, so that we de-risk the roll-out.”
Meanwhile the Road Transport division was clearly the group’s worst performer: revenue essentially flat, at DKr23.4bn; while EBIT before special items decreased 35.1% year on year, to DKr526m, on the back of falling volumes and “a period with operational issues”.
DSV said: “However, the operational performance normalised at the end of the quarter and focus is now shifting to improving productivity and commercial performance.”
It added: “While the Schenker integration continued during the quarter, the synergies are expected to be delayed into 2027.”
In contrast, its Contract Logistics arm saw revenue grow 7.3%, to DKr14.3bn, while EBIT before special items increased 50.3%, to DKr1.7bn, following “productivity and capacity improvements, including consolidation of low-margin sites”.
Mr Lund said: “Where you have activities in warehouses that basically operate at a very low margin, and sometimes even at a minus margin, all these things are not delivering the return we require – we are basically terminating this volume now.
“That’s part of the CL improvement – you take some business out that maybe loses money, or has very low margin, and you replace it with business that operates at a normal margin. And look at what an impact it has,” he added.

The Chinese government has rolled out a set of restrictions on biotechnology ownership transfers, an escalation of oversight from the nation’s government that is seeking to spread the region’s influence on the global biopharmaceutical industry. The restrictions apply to five different types of technology including cell and gene therapy. But licensing deals are excepted, meaning its business as usual for global pharmas.
M&A deals are rare for Chinese sellers, with 91% of all deals so far this year coming from U.S.-based companies. BioSpace Senior Editor Annalee Armstrong spoke to CEO of global investment bank Locust Walk, to put the deal activity on both sides into perspective. While China is undeniably capturing the majority of licensing deals at the moment, U.S. biotechs are enjoying a bumper M&A year.
In the clinic, Disc Medicine reported Phase 3 redemption. In February, the FDA surprised Disc—and the whole biopharma industry, really—by rejecting its lead asset bitopertin for erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP)—a rare disease that causes pain when exposed to the light. This was after previously granting the drug a Commissioner’s National Priority Voucher.
The latest readout showed a reduction in a key biomarker of the disease called PPIX, along with a significant increase in time patients were able to spend in the light. The late-stage trial met all of primary and secondary endpoints, setting the company up for another run at an approval.
Veradermics similarly had a great start to the week, with its oral Rogaine candidate improving hair growth in men during a Phase 3 trial . The data set Veradermics up for an FDA application as well.
And finally, we head to Spain—metaphorically, anyway—to preview the upcoming European Society for Medical Oncology Congress , where antibody-drug conjugates are expected to be the major headline. Merck and partner Kelun-Biotech are expected to present more complete data for sac-TMT; Merck and another partner Moderna will present detailed data on their personalized mRNA vaccine; and Summit Therapeutics and Akeso’s ivonescimab will also get some more time to shine.

Ford Recalls F-Series Trucks for Speedometer and Tachometer Issue
8 photos
Photo: Ford
Imagine pulling a trailer at what you think is 65 miles per hour. The speedo may read 65, then 62, and then stop moving altogether. That is precisely the problem affecting 102,159 trucks from the F-Series, which can be split between the F-150, the HD line, and the medium-duty family of workhorses.
All of these vehicles left their respective factories with analog gauges that may wander erratically or stick in place without warning. 26V653 is what the NHTSA calls this campaign, while 26C46 is Ford's number for it. Both 2025 and 2026 models are potentially affected by the described issue.
The heavier-duty pickups were produced between December 14, 2024, and April 17, 2026, a sole F-750 on November 21, 2025, and the F-150s between August 22, 2025, and May 12, 2026. Supplied by Visteon, the analog cluster modules are listed under a dizzying variety of part numbers in the recall documentation.
Ford claims that supplier process deficiencies are to blame for the reported concern, through the recall filing admits the Dearborn-based automaker still doesn't fully understand the deficiencies at play here. Nevertheless, the supplier allegedly fixed everything with tool maintenance back in January 2026.
As you're well aware, a needle that sticks or moves erratically means the driver loses the primary vehicle speed and engine speed readouts. The Ford Motor Company highlights that customers with a redundant digital speedo may notice a difference between the two displays, and that is the only warning identified by the filing published on the NHTSA's website.
Photo: Ford Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard 101 governs all things controls and displays, and a speedometer that doesn't work as intended can be considered a noncompliance problem. Although certain affected trucks meet the stated requirements, they may not meet the full intent of the rule, thus prompting this recall. The recall population, meanwhile, breaks down rather unevenly.
The heavy- and medium-duty lines are listed with a grand total of 91,589 trucks, starting with a single example of the F-750. The F-600 totals 2,827 units, followed by 12,260 of the F-550, 6,847 of the F-450, 26,354 of the F-350, and 43,300 of the F-250. Add 10,570 units of the F-150 to said figure, and you get 102,159 trucks.
Only 1 percent of the recall population is believed to actually contain the defect. While a small slice of a big number, 1 percent still means over 10,000 trucks at the very least. FoMoCo became aware of this headache back in May 2026, prompted by a growing number of reports alleging sticky or erratic tachs and speedos.
By September 16, the Dearborn-based manufacturer had counted 93 field reports and 18 warranty claims received between January 2025 and August 2026. The remedy comes in the guise of a replacement cluster module, validated for proper operation. Ford isn't ready to say when replacement parts will become widely available at dealers nationwide.
Interim customer letters will be mailed starting on October 26, 2026. Remedy notification letters are likely to follow in the first two weeks of December 2026.

Fast-growing e–commerce logistics provider Stord has made the largest acquisition since its founding 11 years ago, acquiring rival AMS Fulfillment, which processes online orders for more than 150 beauty, wellness and direct-to-consumer brands.
Transaction terms were not disclosed, but Stord said in a news release on Wednesday that the sales price was nine figures.
The deal includes 10 warehouses with nearly 1.3 million square feet of storage, packing and shipping space across Los Angeles, Salt Lake City and Philadelphia, bringing Stord’s global network to more than 100 own-controlled and partner locations, the company announced on Wednesday.
AMS customers are expected to benefit from Stord’s scale and technology in terms of inventory management, speed and reliability.
Stord, which envisions itself as a challenger to Amazon in e-commerce fulfillment, says it processes more than $15 billion annually in gross merchandise value for more than 1,000 e-tailers, many of them small-and-medium enterprises. It increasingly is serving larger brands with high-frequency orders. Revenue has grown 10-fold over the past four years and is approaching $1 billion, according to the company.
Stord provides turnkey services for retailers, managing their inventory across multiple locations, fulfilling orders and selecting carriers for final-mile delivery. It claims it can reach a quarter of U.S. households with timely deliveries.
It secured $650 million in equity and credit capacity this year to support its infrastructure and technology expansion. Earlier this month, Atlanta-based Stord closed a $400 million credit facility and named new chief financial and chief revenue officers. In May, it raised $250 million in venture capital funding that valued the company at $3 billion. The company is using the capital to expand its fulfillment network and accelerate its investment in robotics and artificial intelligence.
Why It Matters: Large fulfillment center operates are trying to gain scale to better compete with Amazon, and other marketplaces like Walmart, that also provide bundled fulfillment and logistics services to third-party sellers.
AMS offers order management, warehouse and inventory management, reverse logistics and other value-added, omni-channel fulfillment services to consumer products companies primarily in the cosmetics, apparel, footwear and accessories sectors. It also provides white-glove services including kitting, displays, and personalization for fulfillment customers.
“AMS brings some of the most discerning brands in the industry onto our platform, and we enter peak season with more scale, intelligence, and momentum than at any point in our history,” CEO and co-founder Sean Henry said.
Henry has previously talked about how he built Stord to give independent brands the physical and digital infrastructure for shipping and fulfillment to compete with Amazon Prime on consumer convenience and cost through a shared platform that no one retailer could build alone.
AMS’s California and Delaware facilities already run automated bin sorting systems, complementing recent investments from Stord’s development hub and giving Stord automated capacity to deploy new robotics and AI.
Stord says its physical infrastructure, combined with vertically integrated technology and a massive and growing dataset, will allow it to train models on live fulfillment data across nearly 100 facilities, leapfrogging normal technology deployment cycles and making the network smarter, faster and cheaper to operate than.
AMS is Stord’s eleventh acquisition. It follows the purchase of Pitney Bowe’s e-commerce fulfillment business in 2024; Ware2Go from UPS and Penny Black, a startup software-as-a-service solution that provides hyper-personalized post-purchase inserts, in 2025; and Shipwire from Ceva Logistics in January. The logistics provider also bought a former Quiet Logistics warehouse this year to expand its footprint in the Dallas market.

SDLG Brasil has completed its first sale in the South American country, delivering an order of six heavy-duty electric wheel loaders to Brazilian mining, construction, and infrastructure company Grupo Base.
Grupo Base ordered four, 27-ton L972 HEV and a pair of, 12.5-ton L938 HEV loaders from Chinese equipment brand Shandong Lingong Construction Machinery Co., Ltd. (the “SD” is “ S han D ong,” the LG is “ L in G ong”) back in June, and the first of the machines are now reportedly on-site, moving dirt, but not making noise.
“ This contract is a historic milestone and comes at a time when we have taken on commercial responsibility for SDLG across 60% of Brazil ,” says Carlos Renato Machado, executive director of SDLG’s Brazilian distributor, Tracbel, before adding that the company hoped to expand the use of electric mining and construction equipment throughout the region .
The machines, themselves
SDLG electric wheel loaders; by Tracbel.
The SDLG machines draw power from 423 and 180 kWh LFP battery packs, respectively, with the larger machines sending power to a 230 kW (~305 hp) electric motor and the smaller machines getting a 180 kW (~240 hp) one. Both specs promise a full day’s worth of continuous operation and fast DC charging between shifts.

Grupo Base operates a fleet of 450 heavy equipment assets at more than 30 concrete and mortar batching plants and 20 crushed stone and fracking sand sites, employing more 2,000 people. The electrification of those assets would represent a massive environmental benefit to the ecologically sensitive region – and that’s a fact not lost on Grupo Base executives .
“We are driving a major transformation across our operations,” says Edson Pechio, president and CEO of Grupo Base, said. “ We want to incorporate solutions that will enable us to operate more efficiently and progressively reduce greenhouse gas emissions .”

Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific (NYSE: UNP ) has announced.
Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit.
“For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP Chief Executive Jim Vena said in release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger , and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.”
Jennifer Hamann (Photo: UP)
Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. She was the executive sponsor of LEAD, the company’s women’s employee resources group, and was recognized by The Manufacturing Institute with a Woman MAKE Award for her contributions to the manufacturing and transportation industries.
“It’s been my honor to serve and represent Union Pacific as its CFO,” Hamann said. “I am grateful for all who supported me along the way — my family, friends and the Union Pacific family I’ve worked alongside for nearly 35 years. Becoming the nation’s first transcontinental railroad is the exciting chapter ahead. I remain an ardent supporter of the merger and with Jim and team leading the way, I’m confident of our success.”
Union Pacific said it will announce succession plans at a later date.
